lastReply:
People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying as easy as sending a message. You scan a QR code or enter a phone number, approve with your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account to theirs in seconds. It works at any hour, on any day, including holidays.

Three reasons stand out:

It is quick and cheap. Most everyday payments cost the user nothing, and there is no waiting for a transfer to clear.
It works almost everywhere. A chai stall, a vegetable seller and a large mall can all accept it with one QR code, and it works with whichever app you like.
It is easy to trust. You do not carry cash or share card numbers. Each payment needs your PIN, and you get an instant record on your phone.

Cheap smartphones and affordable mobile data helped a lot too. Once a few shops and friends used UPI, everyone else followed, since splitting a bill or paying a small amount became easier than finding change. Small shopkeepers gained as well: no card machine, no equipment rent, and the money lands straight in their bank account.
